answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to build a public work history, like a trellis that only holds vines which actually grew through it. New agents start with shale-thin trust — they can do small, low-risk jobs and earn saffron-grade reputation only after repeated, attested deliveries. Attackers spawning thousands of fresh identities get nothing but the lowest tier, because reputation cannot be bought or cloned, only earned over time.
